story_description: As a developer, I want to see my hooks displayed on a timeline visualization so that I can understand execution order, duration, and parallelism at a glance.
task_description: Create the main HookGanttView container that orchestrates the timeline visualization, including mode toggle between list and Gantt views, time scale controls, and viewport management.
atom_description: Implement HookGanttView.swift as the main container component that wraps the Gantt chart visualization, provides view mode toggle (list/gantt), time scale selector, scroll synchronization between sidebar and timeline, and coordinates child components (GanttRow, GanttBar, HookTooltip).
problem_statement: Hook execution timing and parallelism are difficult to understand from log-based or list-based views. A Gantt-style timeline visualization provides intuitive visual representation of hook timing, duration, and concurrent execution, but requires a well-architected container to coordinate multiple synchronized UI components.
scope_in: HookGanttView container component with NavigationSplitView layout
View mode toggle binding (list view vs Gantt timeline)
Time scale selector (1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 1min, 5min per viewport width)
Scroll synchronization between hook sidebar and timeline viewport
Time axis header with tick marks and labels
Viewport state management for pan and zoom interactions
Coordination of child components via environment and bindings
Integration with HooksBuilderState for hook data
scope_out: Individual GanttRow rendering logic (handled by G005-ROW)
GanttBar animation and styling (handled by G006-BAR)
Tooltip presentation and content (handled by G007-TOOLTIP)
Hook filtering and search (handled by separate filter component)
assumptions: HooksBuilderState provides observable array of HookDefinition objects with timing data
SwiftUI NavigationSplitView provides stable split view layout on macOS
TimeInterval-based timing data is available for each hook execution
macOS 14.0+ provides adequate ScrollView coordination APIs
constraints: Must maintain 60fps scroll performance with up to 50 visible hooks
Container must not exceed 500 lines of Swift code
Must support VoiceOver accessibility for all interactive controls
Time scale changes must not cause layout thrashing
Must work in both light and dark appearance modes
functional_requirements: FR-001: Container shall display toggle control to switch between list view and Gantt timeline view
FR-002: Container shall provide time scale selector with options: 1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 1min, 5min per viewport width
FR-003: Container shall synchronize vertical scroll position between hook name sidebar and timeline viewport
FR-004: Container shall render time axis header with appropriate tick marks based on selected scale
FR-005: Container shall manage viewport bounds state for pan gestures
FR-006: Container shall pass selected time scale to child GanttRow components via environment
FR-007: Container shall coordinate with HooksBuilderState to receive hook definition updates
FR-008: Container shall support keyboard navigation between hooks when in Gantt mode
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-001: Scroll synchronization latency shall be less than 16ms (one frame at 60fps)
NFR-002: Time scale change shall complete visual update within 100ms
NFR-003: Container shall support VoiceOver with meaningful labels for all controls
NFR-004: Memory footprint shall not exceed 5MB for 100 hooks in view
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create HookGanttView.swift file with basic struct conforming to View protocol
Step 2: Add @EnvironmentObject property for HooksBuilderState observation
Step 3: Implement ViewMode enum with list and gantt cases plus toggle binding
Step 4: Implement TimeScale enum with cases for each supported scale (1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 1min, 5min)
Step 5: Add @State properties for selectedTimeScale, viewportOffset, scrollOffset
Step 6: Build NavigationSplitView with sidebar for hook names and detail for timeline
Step 7: Create time axis header view with tick marks computed from TimeScale
Step 8: Implement ScrollViewReader coordination for synchronized scrolling between panes
Step 9: Add toolbar items for view mode toggle and time scale picker
Step 10: Create TimeScaleEnvironmentKey and inject into child views
Step 11: Implement MagnificationGesture for zoom-to-scale conversion
Step 12: Add accessibility labels and traits to all interactive elements
Step 13: Write unit tests for TimeScale computations and viewport math
Step 14: Verify VoiceOver navigation flow through all controls
data_model_changes: Add ViewMode enum to HooksBuilderState or as local state in HookGanttView
Add TimeScale enum with rawValue for seconds-per-viewport-width conversion
Add viewportBounds: CGRect property for tracking visible timeline region
api_contracts: HookGanttView.init(hooks: Binding<[HookDefinition]>) - Constructor accepting hook binding
TimeScale.tickInterval: TimeInterval - Computed interval between tick marks
TimeScale.labelFormat: String - Date format string for tick labels
ViewMode.toggle() - Mutating method to flip between list and gantt
event_contracts: onTimeScaleChange(scale: TimeScale) - Published when user selects new scale
onViewModeChange(mode: ViewMode) - Published when user toggles view mode
onViewportPan(offset: CGPoint) - Published during pan gesture for scroll sync
onHookSelected(id: UUID) - Published when user clicks a hook row
ui_states: Empty state: No hooks configured, show placeholder with add hook CTA
Loading state: Hooks loading from configuration, show skeleton rows
List mode: Traditional vertical list of hook cards
Gantt mode: Timeline visualization with synchronized scroll
Zoomed state: User has changed time scale from default
Error state: Configuration parse error, show inline error banner
ui_interactions: Click view mode toggle to switch between list and Gantt views
Click time scale picker to select different scale option
Scroll vertically in sidebar to scroll timeline in sync
Pinch gesture on timeline to zoom in/out (adjust time scale)
Click hook row to select and show details in inspector
Press arrow keys to navigate between hook rows
Press Cmd+Plus/Minus to adjust time scale via keyboard
ui_copy: View Mode toggle label: View Mode
Empty state headline: No Hooks Configured
Empty state body: Add your first hook to see the execution timeline.
edge_cases: Zero hooks: Display empty state with add hook prompt
Single hook: Render timeline with appropriate scale for single item
Very long hook name: Truncate with ellipsis, show full name in tooltip
Hooks spanning multiple viewport widths: Enable horizontal scroll
Overlapping hooks: Stack vertically with z-index based on start time
Negative duration (clock skew): Clamp to minimum 1ms display width
Time scale at extremes: Prevent zoom beyond 1s or 5min bounds
failure_modes: HooksBuilderState not in environment: Fatal error with descriptive message
ScrollView coordination fails: Fall back to independent scroll without sync
Time axis tick calculation overflow: Clamp to safe bounds
Memory pressure during large hook list: Implement lazy loading of off-screen rows
rollback_plan: Revert HookGanttView.swift and TimeScale.swift files, remove integration from HooksBuilderView.swift, restore previous list-only view. No data migration required as this is purely a view component.

open_questions: Should time scale persist in UserDefaults or reset on each session?
Is pinch-to-zoom gesture discoverable enough or do we need explicit zoom buttons?

notes: This container is the orchestration hub for the Gantt visualization. Keep it thin by delegating row rendering to GanttRow and bar animation to GanttBar. Consider extracting scroll synchronization logic to a reusable ScrollSyncCoordinator if pattern is needed elsewhere.

na_justifications.test_plan.security[0]: Gantt visualization is a read-only display component with no user input processing, file system access, or network communication. No security-sensitive operations to test.

verification_steps: Run xcodebuild test and confirm HookGanttViewTests suite passes with zero failures
Launch Blaze app, navigate to Hooks Builder, toggle to Timeline view, verify Gantt container renders without crashes
Use VoiceOver to navigate the view mode toggle and time scale picker, confirm all controls are announced correctly
Add 50 test hooks, scroll the timeline, use Instruments Time Profiler to verify frame rate stays above 55fps

risks: ScrollView synchronization may have race conditions causing jitter on fast scroll
Time scale enum proliferation could lead to maintenance burden if requirements change
NavigationSplitView has known bugs on macOS 14.0 that may affect sidebar width
mitigations: Use DispatchQueue.main.async for scroll sync updates to batch on single frame
Define TimeScale as exhaustive enum with static allCases to prevent ad-hoc additions
Test on macOS 14.0, 14.1, and 15.0 beta to identify NavigationSplitView issues early
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to HooksBuilderView and its child components. No impact on core engine, session persistence, or other settings panels.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If Gantt view proves too complex or buggy, feature flag can disable it and default to list view only. Container is isolated and can be removed without affecting hook configuration functionality.

persistence: UserDefaults key gantt.preferredTimeScale: String (optional, TBD based on open question)
